messages.text: just feeling so drained lately, like no matter how much i do, it doesn't matter

It sounds like you’ve been carrying a lot, and it’s leaving you feeling worn out and maybe disconnected from any sense of progress. That can be a sign of emotional exhaustion, which often happens when stress builds without enough rest or support. Can you share what’s been taking most of your energy lately?
classes mostly. and just like... keeping up with everything. feels like i'm running in place

That “running in place” feeling can be really discouraging, especially when you’re putting in effort but not feeling forward momentum. Academic pressures combined with daily responsibilities can drain mental and physical energy quickly. Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, mood, or motivation alongside this?
sleep’s been okay? i mean, not great, but it’s fine. i’ve had worse

Even “okay” sleep can still leave you tired if stress is high, because rest quality matters as much as quantity. When you’re under constant pressure, your mind may not fully switch off, which can keep you feeling drained. Would you like to explore small ways to create more mental space or recovery during your day?
maybe. i just feel like i'm stuck, y'know? like i'm doing all this stuff but for what?

That sense of “what’s the point” can sometimes be linked to burnout or feeling disconnected from your own goals and values. It might help to pause and reflect on what matters most to you, beyond the immediate tasks. Do you think your current workload aligns with what you want in the long term?
i keep coming back to this feeling like... what's the point? i'm grinding through school, but after that? no idea. and honestly... sometimes i don't even want a after that

It sounds like you’re feeling not just overwhelmed, but also uncertain about your future and why you’re pushing forward. That loss of motivation can sometimes be accompanied by hopelessness, and I want to make sure you’re safe. Are you experiencing thoughts about not wanting to live or harming yourself?
yeah... sometimes i think it’s not. like, what’s the point of building a future if it’s just more of this?

Thank you for sharing that—these thoughts are important and deserve care. When you feel hopeless, it can be hard to see alternatives, but you don’t have to navigate this alone. Are you currently thinking about hurting yourself or making plans to do so?
no no, i'm not gonna do anything. just... wish i didn't feel this way, y'know?

I’m relieved to hear you’re not planning to harm yourself, and it’s still important to address the weight of these feelings. Hopelessness can improve when you have support and small steps toward meaning, even if it’s not clear right now. Would you be open to talking about what’s been most heavy lately so we can figure out ways to lighten it?
i used to think about it a lot more... like, all the time. but therapy and this program have helped a little. still hard though

It’s encouraging that therapy and this program have helped reduce how often those thoughts come, even if the heaviness remains. Progress can be gradual, and it’s okay to still struggle while you’re working on it. What feels most supportive for you right now—connection, coping strategies, or something else?
is it normal to still feel this... empty? even though i'm trying? feels like i should be further along by now

Yes, it’s quite common to still feel empty even when you’re actively working on yourself—healing isn’t linear. Sometimes the effort doesn’t bring immediate relief, but it’s still laying the groundwork for change. Would you like to explore what “empty” feels like for you and what might gently fill those spaces?
part of me wants to believe things can get better... but another part just wants to give up. like, why keep fighting if nothing changes?

That tug-of-war between hope and wanting to give up can be exhausting, and it’s a sign you’re carrying a lot internally. Sometimes change is slow and hard to see until you look back later, but holding on allows for the possibility of those shifts. What has helped you lean toward the hopeful side, even briefly?
i don’t know what to do right now... but is there something small? like, anything i can do to feel less like this?

One small step could be doing something that grounds you in the present—like focusing on your senses, taking a short walk, or connecting with someone you trust. Even a few minutes of intentional breathing or listening to a calming sound can create a bit of space from the heaviness. Would you like me to guide you through a simple grounding exercise right now?
yeah... okay. i’ll try. can you guide me?

Alright, let’s try a short grounding exercise. Sit comfortably, take a slow breath in through your nose, and feel your lungs expand. As you exhale, look around and name five things you can see, four things you can touch, three things you can hear, two things you can smell, and one thing you can taste. How do you feel after going through that?
i did it... naming everything. it helped a little? i feel kinda more here, but still tired. still sad. but... not as foggy

That’s a good sign—feeling “more here” means you’ve connected with the present, even if the sadness is still there. Sometimes these exercises are less about erasing feelings and more about making them manageable. Would you like to keep building a few more small tools you can use when the fog starts creeping back?
thanks for... y'know, not judging me. it helps just to say it out loud sometimes

You’re welcome, and I’m glad you felt it was safe to share. Talking openly can make a heavy burden feel a little lighter. Would you like to use this space to keep saying what’s on your mind without having to hold it back?
i’ll try to do that grounding thing when i start feeling foggy again. not sure i’ll remember, but i’ll try

That’s a great intention, and even trying is a step forward. You could jot it down somewhere or set a gentle reminder on your phone to make it easier to remember. Would you like me to suggest a short phrase you can use as a cue for grounding?
yeah, that could help. sometimes i just need a little nudge

How about using the phrase “right here, right now” as your cue? Saying it quietly or in your head can remind you to notice your surroundings and breathe. Do you want me to pair it with a quick, two-breath grounding method so it’s even easier to use?
yes, please. that sounds like something i might actually use

When you say “right here, right now,” take one slow breath in, noticing what you see in front of you, then exhale and feel your feet on the ground. On the second breath in, focus on one sound you hear, and exhale feeling a little more present. This can be done anywhere and only takes about ten seconds. Would you like me to help you practice it once together?
yeah, let’s do it once together. i think that’ll help me remember

Okay, let’s begin.  
Say quietly to yourself: *“Right here, right now.”*  
Take a slow breath in, notice what you see, then exhale and feel your feet on the ground.  
Now breathe in again, focus on one sound you hear, and as you exhale, let yourself feel anchored in this moment—how does that feel?
just did it... “right here, right now.” felt kinda silly at first, but actually helped. i feel a little more... here. less floaty

That’s a great result, and it’s completely fine if it felt a bit silly at first—many helpful tools do. The important part is that it brought you back and reduced that floaty feeling. Would you like to make this phrase and exercise part of your daily routine so it becomes second nature?
i’ll try to use it when i start feeling floaty again. not sure i’ll remember every time, but i’ll keep it in my pocket, y’know?

That sounds like a good plan—having it “in your pocket” gives you something steady to reach for when things feel off. Each time you use it, you reinforce the habit, even if you forget sometimes. Would you like to pair this with one other small practice to help with the tired, heavy feeling?
yeah... anything else that’s not too much? like, something small i can actually do

One small thing you could try is “micro-breaks”—pausing for one to two minutes between tasks to stretch, drink water, or step outside. These moments can help your body and mind reset without needing big chunks of time. Do you think this could fit into your day without feeling like another chore?
yeah, that sounds doable. i can at least try to step outside for a sec between classes

That’s a great start—just a quick breath of fresh air can make a noticeable difference over time. Pairing it with your grounding cue could make it even more impactful. Would you like me to help you create a simple routine combining both?
i’ll try doing the phrase when i step outside between classes. like a little reset button

That sounds like a strong, practical plan—a quick step outside plus “right here, right now” can give you both physical and mental reset. Over time, those small resets may help lower the heaviness and fog. Do you want to check in next time on how it’s working for you?
thanks... for walking me through this. i don’t feel as alone right now, and that means a lot

I’m really glad you feel less alone—that connection is important, especially when things feel heavy. Your willingness to try these small steps shows real strength. Would you like to wrap up with one more grounding breath together, so you leave this space feeling steady?
yeah, let’s do one more. “right here, right now”... breathe in, breathe out. okay. i’m here.

Exactly—you’re here, and you’ve taken steps to anchor yourself despite the heaviness. Holding onto that moment of presence can be a reminder you can return to whenever needed. I’m glad we practiced together today, and you’re not alone in this. Would you like to keep building on these tools next time?
yeah, i’ll keep trying this. and i’ll come back next time. thanks for... everything

You’re welcome, and I’m glad you’ll keep trying—it’s the small, steady steps that add up over time. I’ll be here when you come back, ready to keep building on what works for you. Take care of yourself until then.
